solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Argue over daughter's news

indicators.note: in an across clue 'over' asks for the verb to be turned round, read from the other end

parts.note: to row is to argue noisily
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter; the 's just links

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over what a daughter has told the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Word means tidings or information, as in 'any word from her?', so it is a synonym of news.

clue.text: Paperwork from folders

parts.note: paperwork read literally as work made of paper, by folders who fold rather than office files

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests office files; the cryptic reading is craft work done by people folding paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of folding paper into shapes is literally work in paper made by folding.

clue.text: Romeo, having popped off outside, stopped being soppy

indicators.note: the word for 'popped off' sits outside, wrapping round the letter for Romeo

parts.note: R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A romantic hero dies and his mushy sentiment finally comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soppy' looks like sentimental, but here it means soaking wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soppy is wet through, so once it has dried it is no longer sodden.

clue.text: Inventor of old boat was originally correct

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a ship's inventor got it right.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright invented the water frame for spinning cotton in 18th-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkwright was the English industrialist who devised the spinning frame, an inventor of the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Foul, interminable canal seepage disheartened part of the Med

indicators.note: foul as in fouled up, so the letters are muddled into a new order
without its terminals, the two end letters are dropped
the heart, the central letter, is removed

explanation.surface: Filthy water leaking from a canal ends up polluting the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean lying between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: Means to decode unknown interrupting energy signal

indicators.note: the unknown breaks into the sequence of energy and signal, splitting them

parts.note: KE is the physics abbreviation for kinetic energy
to give the word is to give a signal
algebra calls unknowns x, y and z

explanation.surface: A spy waits for the codebreaking signal that cuts through the static.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyword unlocks a cipher: knowing it lets you decipher the coded message.

clue.text: Section of flight concerning gent in a spin?

indicators.note: spinning round turns the combined letters back to front

parts.note: sir is how a gentleman is addressed

explanation.surface: A passenger worries about a man whose aircraft is spinning out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of each step in a staircase, so it forms part of the stairs.

clue.text: Woman to whom links might portend loneliness

definitions.text: Woman to whom links might portend loneliness

parts.words: Woman to whom links might portend loneliness
parts.note: links are seaside golf courses, which keep her husband away all day and leave her alone

explanation.walkthrough: Links sound like bonds or connections, which ought to prevent loneliness; here they are seaside golf courses.
explanation.definitionFit: The jokey term for a wife regularly abandoned while her spouse spends his free time on the course.

clue.text: Bore not quite following 10's thread

parts.note: the cross-reference number, read simply as ten

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to drill is to bore a hole

explanation.surface: A dull person almost follows the plot of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to clue 10's answer, but it is just the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender threadlike shoot a climbing plant uses to cling.

clue.text: Sharply swinging both ways, aquiver

parts.note: slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: A pendulum moves briskly back and forth, trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitingly describes remarks made cuttingly, with a sharp sting, so it means pointedly or sharply.

clue.text: Regularly slip by fast mum

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, the first and third

parts.note: only its odd letters are used
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A mother keeps quietly sneaking past during her fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it means saying nothing, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum is an adjective meaning not speaking.

clue.text: Punishment once upset lad in refuge

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for refuge

parts.note: a harbour is a place of shelter

indicators.note: an upset tips things over, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A troubled boy once found shelter as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour was a former criminal sentence of heavy physical work, abolished in Britain in 1948.

clue.text: Exhausted by choice between diametrically opposite points?

indicators.note: the word for a choice is placed between the two compass letters

parts.note: west and east, compass points facing each other
or offers a choice of alternatives

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out by having to choose between opposite directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Wore can mean wore out, used up or tired, so it stands for exhausted as a verb.

clue.text: Cable with uninitiated rental

indicators.note: without its initial, the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A cable company signs up a customer who knows nothing about renting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is a metal cable carrying current or signals, and a cable is also a telegram, as is a wire.

clue.text: Privately tipped focus ahead of common sense

indicators.note: the first part comes before the second in a down entry
with its tip, the top letter in a down clue, removed

parts.note: a centre is a focal point

explanation.surface: A confidential tip says to concentrate before using one's judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' suggests a racing tip, but means losing the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, i.e. in confidence, which is what privately means.

clue.text: Team Blue led off, up to the left or right

definitions.text: up to the left or right

indicators.note: off as in gone off or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team in blue was led off the pitch by a sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' means mounted on a horse: riding with both legs to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle a rider is mounted with both legs to one side of the horse, left or right.

clue.text: Scratching backside, Russian almost tore damaged muscle

indicators.note: the combined letters are broken up and rearranged
scratching out the rear letter of a word
the word stops one letter short

explanation.surface: A Russian scratching his bottom nearly tore a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sartorius is the long thigh muscle, the longest in the human body, sometimes called the tailor's muscle.

clue.text: Best, eg, to label for moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ideal choice is to put a label on something before moving it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is George Best, the Manchester United and Northern Ireland winger.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best is a famous example of a soccer player, so Best is one instance of the answer.

clue.text: Satisfactory, to some extent unending, Pacific campaign

indicators.note: without an end, the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A war campaign in the Pacific was, in some respects, acceptable and never-ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Okinawa in 1945 was a major Second World War campaign fought on that Pacific island.

clue.text: What may pursue snakes and large snakes

explanation.surface: Some board-game piece chasing serpents, both small and large.
explanation.walkthrough: The board game Snakes and Ladders always names snakes first, so ladders follow them.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game name, the second item comes after the snakes, following them in the title.

clue.text: Decapitated pig's dark-red

indicators.note: with the head cut off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a pig is a swine; the 's is just possessive

explanation.surface: A beheaded pig's blood is a deep red.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is a colour name for a deep purplish red, like that of red wine.

clue.text: Uncovered penniless, desperate composer

indicators.note: in a desperate state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
with its covering, the outer letters, stripped off

parts.note: used without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A poor composer, exposed and broke, is desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was the Danish composer of six symphonies, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Square equals two thirds of six?

definitions.meaning: a square number, three times three
the last two of the three letters of SIX spell IX

explanation.walkthrough: The arithmetic looks like it gives four, but it means two thirds of the word SIX.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three squared, and IX is how the Romans wrote that number.

clue.text: Knocked south, losing seconds in unfavourable sea

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for the sea
the letter is lost from the word

explanation.surface: A ship heading south loses time in an unfriendly sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something is to criticise it, as does to badmouth it, so the past forms match.

clue.text: Final 60% of extra pay rises for petty officer

indicators.note: points to the last three of the five letters, which are the part that moves
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so that part is turned round

explanation.surface: A pay bonus goes up for a junior naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last three letters of the bonus word are turned round; the first two stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, or boatswain, is a ship's officer in charge of equipment, ranking as a petty officer.

clue.text: Mathematician shunning grand city on the Po

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the letter for grand is left out

parts.note: Alan Turing, the British codebreaker and computing pioneer
G is slang for a thousand pounds, a grand

explanation.surface: A mathematician avoids a grand city on an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, Torino in Italian, is the Piedmont capital standing on the River Po.

clue.text: Fliers returning over El Salvador's islands

indicators.note: going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
ES is the country code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: Airmen fly home over a Central American country's islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroes are a group of North Atlantic islands between Shetland and Iceland, belonging to Denmark.

clue.text: Journalist resisted sports

indicators.note: to sport can mean to frolic about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A reporter refused to cover the sports pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a dated term for a female editor, a senior newspaper journalist.

clue.text: Boy is into creative subjects, those hiding a burning desire?

indicators.note: the boy and is go into the word for creative subjects

explanation.surface: A boy is drawn to the arts, nursing a secret passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' sounds like an intense longing; here it is a literal urge to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsonists are fire-raisers who deliberately set fire to property, a literal desire to see things burn.

clue.text: Girl moaning about hugs

indicators.note: turned about, so the hidden letters read backwards
the outer word hugs the letters, holding them inside it

parts.note: the word containing the answer, back to front

explanation.surface: A girl grumbles about being hugged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword terms.
